Each notebook tells its story in words, pictures, math and code. Before you run a cell, guess what it will print or draw, and then run it to find out. The surprises are where the learning happens.

**Keep your work.** Colab does not save a notebook opened from the links below. Once it is open, choose **File**, then **Save a copy in Drive**, and work in your copy. Your changes will be waiting the next time you open it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
import sys, tomllib
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "tools")
from nbutil import student_notebooks, load, text, NOTEBOOKS

repo = tomllib.loads(Path("course.toml").read_text())["repository"]
url, ref = repo["url"].rstrip("/"), repo["ref"]
github = url.startswith("https://github.com/") and "CHANGE-ME" not in url

print("| Notebook | Read | Run in Colab |")
print("| --- | --- | --- |")
for path in student_notebooks():
    first = text(load(path)["cells"][0]).splitlines()[0].lstrip("# ").strip()
    page = path.relative_to(Path.cwd()).with_suffix(".html").as_posix()
    if github:
        colab = f"https://colab.research.google.com/github/{url.removeprefix('https://github.com/')}/blob/{ref}/notebooks/{path.name}"
        run = f"[Open in Colab]({colab})"
    else:
        run = "*after the repository is published*"
    print(f"| {first} | [web page]({page}) | {run} |")
```

Each notebook page also links a PDF version.

**Why start at 0?** Two reasons. Zero is where everyone starts. And computers count from 0, too: in Python, the first item in a list is `my_list[0]`.

The [Angle Explorer](angle-explorer.qmd) is the drawing tool behind `explore_angles`.
